salt.title: Dry road salt applied
salt.desc: Dry road salt used by the state highway agency per state-owned lane-mile. Municipal application and liquid brine are outside this reading.
salt.method: Divides reported US short tons of dry salt by 2022 state-owned lane-miles. One winter. States that did not report remain unshaded.
salt.note: State average over the state-owned network.

coast5.title: Residents within 5 km of the sea
coast5.desc: Share of county residents represented by populated tract centers within 5 km of an ocean or marine bay. Wind and shelter change local exposure.
coast5.method: Distance from each populated Census tract’s population center to the Natural Earth marine coastline. Sum tract populations inside a 5 km threshold and divide by county population. Great Lakes excluded. The 5 km cutoff illustrates proximity.
coast5.note: The 5 km band is a proximity proxy.

coastkm.title: Mean distance to saltwater coast
coastkm.desc: Population-weighted distance between Census tract centers and the nearest mapped marine coastline. Darker shading marks closer locations.
coastkm.method: Length is approximate great-circle distance. It covers coasts in the U.S., Canada and Mexico. Census tract population weights locate residences within large counties.

hh.title: Humid heat
hh.desc: Hours with air temperature ≥27°C (81°F) and relative humidity ≥70% at the same time.
hh.method: Hours with air temperature ≥27°C (81°F) and relative humidity ≥70% at the same time. Nearest qualifying station to the county internal point. TMY3 assembles 12 historical representative months from 15- or 30-year archives; this is a typical weather year and cannot reconstruct a particular ownership period.
hh.note: Station-based estimate for the county reference point.

wet.title: Atmospheric wetness proxy
wet.desc: Hours with air temperature >0°C and relative humidity >80%. This estimates conditions favorable to surface wetness. Rain, dew and vehicle shelter can change actual wetness.
wet.method: Hours with air temperature >0°C and relative humidity >80%. This estimates conditions favorable to surface wetness. Rain, dew and vehicle shelter can change actual wetness. Nearest qualifying station to the county internal point. TMY3 assembles 12 historical representative months from 15- or 30-year archives; this is a typical weather year and cannot reconstruct a particular ownership period.
wet.note: Station-based estimate for the county reference point.

highrh.title: High relative humidity
highrh.desc: Hours with relative humidity above 80%, at any temperature.
highrh.method: Hours with relative humidity above 80%, at any temperature. Nearest TMY3 station with complete hourly readings.
highrh.note: Station-based estimate for the county reference point.

hoth.title: Heat at or above 35°C
hoth.method: Hours with station air temperature ≥35°C (95°F). Nearest qualifying station to the county internal point. TMY3 assembles 12 historical representative months from 15- or 30-year archives; this is a typical weather year and cannot reconstruct a particular ownership period.
hoth.note: Station-based estimate for the county reference point.

solar.title: Solar energy at ground level
solar.desc: Annual mean daily global horizontal solar irradiation. Outdoor solar energy serves as a proxy for sun exposure. UV dose and indoor parking require additional information.
solar.method: Annual mean daily global horizontal solar irradiation. Outdoor solar energy serves as a proxy for sun exposure. UV dose and indoor parking require additional information. Nearest qualifying station to the county internal point. TMY3 assembles 12 historical representative months from 15- or 30-year archives; this is a typical weather year and cannot reconstruct a particular ownership period.
solar.note: Station-based estimate for the county reference point.

coldh.title: Hours at or below −18°C
coldh.desc: Hours with outdoor air temperature at or below −18°C (about 0°F) in the matched typical year.
coldh.method: Hours with outdoor air temperature at or below −18°C (about 0°F) in the matched typical year. TMY3 represents ordinary seasonal patterns. NOAA 30-year normals are preferable for frequent extreme thresholds.
coldh.note: Station-based estimate for the county reference point.

hot90.title: Days reaching 90°F
hot90.desc: Average days each year when the daily high reaches at least 90°F.
hot90.method: Average days each year when the daily high reaches at least 90°F. Each county internal point is matched to the nearest station with standard NOAA completeness flags in the five temperature inputs. Freeze–thaw days equal the count of nights ≤32°F minus days with a maximum ≤32°F.
hot90.note: 30-year climate normal at the matched station.

hot100.title: Days reaching 100°F
hot100.desc: Average days each year when the daily high reaches at least 100°F.
hot100.method: Average days each year when the daily high reaches at least 100°F. Each county internal point is matched to the nearest station with standard NOAA completeness flags in the five temperature inputs. Freeze–thaw days equal the count of nights ≤32°F minus days with a maximum ≤32°F.
hot100.note: 30-year climate normal at the matched station.

ft.title: Freeze–thaw days
ft.desc: Average days with a low at or below 32°F and a high above 32°F. Air temperature is a proxy for vehicle-surface temperature.
ft.method: Average days with a low at or below 32°F and a high above 32°F. Air temperature is a proxy for vehicle-surface temperature. Each county internal point is matched to the nearest station with standard NOAA completeness flags in the five temperature inputs. Freeze–thaw days equal the count of nights ≤32°F minus days with a maximum ≤32°F.
ft.note: 30-year climate normal at the matched station.

cold0.title: Nights reaching 0°F or colder
cold0.desc: Average days per year when the minimum reaches 0°F or colder. Cold-start counts depend on when the vehicle was driven.
cold0.method: Average days per year when the minimum reaches 0°F or colder. Cold-start counts depend on when the vehicle was driven. Each county internal point is matched to the nearest station with standard NOAA completeness flags in the five temperature inputs. Freeze–thaw days equal the count of nights ≤32°F minus days with a maximum ≤32°F.
cold0.note: 30-year climate normal at the matched station.

steep.title: Road miles at ≥4.5% grade
steep.desc: Share of grade-classified road miles with absolute grade of at least 4.5%. Both uphill and downhill miles contribute.
steep.method: Assign official HPMS grade A–F mileages to county-contained route intervals. Reconcile category-mile totals with interval lengths, reject ambiguous overlaps, and merge repeated values across adjoining subdivisions only when their combined length matches. The numerator counts absolute grades ≥4.5%, classes D–F. The sample contains major roads in both directions. No continuous descent length or traffic weighting. The state display additionally requires 100 accepted miles and 10 accepted intervals with sufficient grade-class reporting.
steep.note: Measured sample largely covers major roads.

urban.title: Population living in urban areas
urban.desc: Share of county residents in Census-defined urban areas. It gives a nationwide proxy for stop-and-go exposure.
urban.method: 2020 Census urban population divided by total county population. Local roads, commute patterns and trip times can differ considerably within this area. The value cannot be converted directly to stops, brake applications or idle time.

brake.title: Hard-braking events
brake.desc: Hard-braking events per 1,000 miles in the participating city’s Drivewise sample. Normal stops and braking energy require separate measurements.
brake.method: 2019 Allstate report using opt-in Drivewise observations from 2016–17. Points locate 125 city or Census-designated place centers with published rates in the contiguous U.S. Only observed places are shown. A city point displayed for a county identifies its location and does not extend its rate to the whole county.
brake.note: City point observations. Gray land falls outside the point sample.

rough.title: Rough federal-aid road miles
rough.desc: Share of rated federal-aid network miles with poor ride quality. The proportion of the network rated varies by state.
rough.method: Poor = International Roughness Index >170 in/mi or Present Serviceability Rating <2.6 in FHWA HM-47I. The denominator is rated network mileage. Check reporting coverage before comparing states.

roughcov.title: Federal-aid pavement rating coverage
roughcov.desc: Share of federal-aid network mileage included in the state pavement ratings. Larger values mean more complete measurements.
roughcov.method: Reported mileage divided by reported plus unreported mileage as tabulated in HM-47I.

unpaved.title: Unpaved local-road miles
unpaved.desc: Share of reported local public road mileage classified as unpaved. This measures the chance of encountering unpaved roads on the network.
unpaved.method: FHWA HM-51 rural and urban local-system miles, combined. Does not weight routes by traffic or estimate dust concentrations. Both rural and urban local mileage totals must be reported.

flood.title: Flood report days
flood.desc: Distinct dates with one or more county-coded flood or flash-flood reports. A report can involve only part of the county.
flood.method: Unique local begin dates per county across 10 calendar years. NOAA types Flood and Flash Flood. Excludes forecast-zone reports, including coastal-flood categories, and events without a county code. A zero records no qualifying report. Reporting intensity and county size affect comparisons; vehicle damage requires its own evidence.

hail.title: Hail report days
hail.desc: Distinct dates with one or more county-coded hail reports. A report can involve only part of the county.
hail.method: Unique local begin dates per county across 10 calendar years. NOAA types Hail. Excludes forecast-zone reports, including coastal-flood categories, and events without a county code. A zero records no qualifying report. Reporting intensity and county size affect comparisons; vehicle damage requires its own evidence.

seaSalt.title: Airborne fine sea salt
seaSalt.desc: Five-year mean outdoor concentration of sea salt in the fine-particle fraction. Larger particles, vehicle deposits and road spray require different measurements.
seaSalt.method: Satellite, chemical transport model and ground-monitor estimates. Within each 2017 county, average valid 0.01° grid cells with latitude-dependent area weights, then average five annual estimates equally. Adapted from Siyuan Shen and coauthors, Washington University ACAG, CC BY 4.0.

dust.title: Airborne fine mineral dust
dust.desc: Five-year mean outdoor concentration of mineral dust in the fine-particle fraction. Larger particles, vehicle deposits and road spray require different measurements.
dust.method: Satellite, chemical transport model and ground-monitor estimates. Within each 2017 county, average valid 0.01° grid cells with latitude-dependent area weights, then average five annual estimates equally. Adapted from Siyuan Shen and coauthors, Washington University ACAG, CC BY 4.0.

delay.title: Traffic delay per auto commuter
delay.desc: Annual excess travel time per auto commuter. A delay includes moving slowly and waiting.
delay.method: Annual excess travel time per auto commuter. A delay includes moving slowly and waiting. Texas A&M Transportation Institute 2025 Urban Mobility Report. The point locates the lead city or a Census urban-area reference point. The value applies to the wider urban area. Time spent stopped and brake counts require separate measurements.
delay.note: Urban-area observations shown at reference points.

peak.title: Peak travel in congestion
peak.desc: Share of peak-period vehicle-miles traveled in congested conditions. Only areas with a published value are shown.
peak.method: Share of peak-period vehicle-miles traveled in congested conditions. Only areas with a published value are shown. Texas A&M Transportation Institute 2025 Urban Mobility Report. The point locates the lead city or a Census urban-area reference point. The value applies to the wider urban area. Time spent stopped and brake counts require separate measurements.
peak.note: Urban-area observations shown at reference points.

roughLocal.title: Rough miles on sampled major roads
roughLocal.desc: Share of eligible major-road mileage with measured roughness above 170 inches per mile. Local streets and ramps are outside the sample.
roughLocal.method: Sum eligible section lengths with International Roughness Index >170 in/mi and divide by the sum of section lengths with a positive IRI. FHWA functional classes 1–5 and one-/two-way facilities only. Weights use inventoried miles, independent of traffic.

snow.title: Days with ≥1 inch of snowfall
snow.desc: Average days per year with at least one inch of new snow. Plowing and salt treatment vary by jurisdiction.
snow.method: Nearest qualifying NOAA snow station to the county internal point, subject to a 150 km maximum. This is snowfall frequency. A winter salt rate measures a different condition.
snow.note: Snow observations farther than 150 km are unshaded.

wiSalt.title: Wisconsin county salt use
wiSalt.desc: Reported salt application per state-highway lane-mile in each Wisconsin county. Coverage is limited to the state system and this winter.
wiSalt.method: WisDOT annual report, table 1.4, all 72 Wisconsin counties. The map displays the listed rate, with county totals and lane mileage in the research data.

rugged.title: Terrain variation along roads
rugged.desc: Mean USDA road Terrain Ruggedness Index. Higher values indicate larger elevation differences between nearby cells that contain roads.
rugged.method: Uses the 2020-vintage USDA ERS tract file with a 2024 road network. County mean weights each tract’s mean Road TRI by its RoadTRI_Count grid cells. Separate nearby roads may differ in elevation. This terrain proxy does not yield road grade or descent length.
rugged.note: Terrain ruggedness for road-containing grid cells.

gradeLocal.title: Sampled miles at ≥4.5% grade
gradeLocal.desc: Share of sampled road mileage with absolute grade ≥4.5%. Values require ≥10 accepted miles and at least three accepted intervals in the county.
gradeLocal.method: Assign official HPMS grade A–F mileages to county-contained route intervals. Reconcile category-mile totals with interval lengths, reject ambiguous overlaps, and merge repeated values across adjoining subdivisions only when their combined length matches. The numerator counts absolute grades ≥4.5%, classes D–F. The sample contains major roads in both directions. No continuous descent length or traffic weighting.
gradeLocal.note: County estimates require ≥10 audited miles across ≥3 intervals.

roadPM10.title: Dust emitted from unpaved roads
roadPM10.desc: Modeled primary PM₁₀ emissions from unpaved roads per square mile of county land. This is an emission rate, separate from ambient dust concentration.
roadPM10.method: Filter EPA NEI to primary PM10, unpaved-road dust and annual county totals, excluding separately listed tribal rows. Divide reported short tons per year by 2020 Census county land area. Missing entries remain blank.

snowCover.title: Monthly snow-cover frequency
snowCover.desc: Share of observed land days classified as snow-covered in the selected month. This records snow persistence around the county reference point. Road plowing changes the surface a car encounters.
snowCover.method: Reuses the terrain atlas IMS 24 km snow series on its 0.25° overview grid. Sample the cell containing the county reference point, with no gap filling. Average 20 month-year frequencies, each with at least 80% observed calendar days. Zero and missing are distinct.
snowCover.note: The month selector changes the snow-cover map.

monthlyHigh.title: Monthly average daily high
monthlyHigh.desc: Average daily high for the selected month. The calendar month is averaged over 20 historical years.
monthlyHigh.method: Reuses the terrain atlas monthly nClimGrid climate grids. Its 2 × 2 native-cell aggregation requires 20 years for each contributing cell. Sample the overview cell at each county reference point without filling missing coverage; convert Celsius to Fahrenheit.
monthlyHigh.note: Typical daily temperature for the selected month.

monthlyLow.title: Monthly average daily low
monthlyLow.desc: Average daily low for the selected month. The calendar month is averaged over 20 historical years.
monthlyLow.method: Reuses the terrain atlas monthly nClimGrid climate grids. Its 2 × 2 native-cell aggregation requires 20 years for each contributing cell. Sample the overview cell at each county reference point without filling missing coverage; convert Celsius to Fahrenheit.
monthlyLow.note: Typical daily temperature for the selected month.

landSlope.title: Regional land-surface slope
landSlope.desc: Mean slope of the surrounding land in the cell containing the county reference point. Compare it with road-only ruggedness and measured road grades.
landSlope.method: Reuses the terrain atlas USGS 3DEP processing. Horn 3 × 3 gradients on 500 m elevation samples were averaged into 0.05° display cells. Approximate cell height 5.6 km. This measures regional topography and cannot describe the grade or direction of a vehicle’s route.

snowYear.title: Snow-covered days in a typical year
snowYear.desc: Expected days of mapped snow cover over a typical calendar year.
snowYear.method: Multiply each monthly IMS snow-cover fraction by the average number of calendar days in that month during 2006–2025, then sum January through December. All 12 months must be observed. Snow on land measures a different exposure from salt applied to roads.

floodYear.title: Flood report days per year
floodYear.desc: Average number of days per year with one or more qualifying reports.
floodYear.method: Divide the ten-year count of distinct reported event dates by ten. County size and reporting intensity affect this measure.

hailYear.title: Hail report days per year
hailYear.desc: Average number of days per year with one or more qualifying reports.
hailYear.method: Divide the ten-year count of distinct reported event dates by ten. County size and reporting intensity affect this measure.

annualExposure.title: Annual exposure score
annualExposure.desc: Higher scores indicate greater combined exposure across the eleven categories. The U.S. county average is 50.
annualExposure.method: Rank each indicator against counties with data, splitting ties at the midpoint. Average ranks within each category, then average the eleven categories equally. A missing indicator receives 50. The missing-data range uses 0 and 100 instead. The weights describe exposure and have not been fitted to vehicle inspections or repair bills.
annualExposure.note: 50 is the county average. Each exposure category carries the same weight.

additional_fields.snow_site: NOAA source station ID for snowfall
additional_fields.gradeMi: Audited grade miles before county minimum thresholds
additional_fields.gradeN: Audited grade interval count before county minimum thresholds
additional_fields.ratedMi: Miles of eligible road sections with measured roughness
additional_fields.noaa_km: Distance from county internal point to NOAA station (km)
additional_fields.tmy_km: Distance from county internal point to TMY3 station (km)
